prompt_text: Who is the best interior painting company in St. Louis MO?
answer_verbatim:
I can’t look up live local rankings from here, so I can’t name a single “best” interior painter in St. Louis right now. What I can do is help you find the best one for your needs and avoid poor choices. A few quick questions so I can give targeted recommendations:

- Is this for a house (single-family), condo, apartment, or commercial space?
- Which St. Louis neighborhood or ZIP code?
- How many rooms / approximate square footage and any prep work (wall repair, popcorn ceiling removal, trim/cabinet painting)?
- Budget and timeline?
- Do you want eco-friendly or low-VOC paints, and any special finishes?

If you want to proceed on your own, use this step-by-step process and checklist to identify the best option:

Where to look
- Google Maps, Yelp, Angi (formerly Angie’s List), Houzz, and the BBB for local companies and review summaries.
- Facebook community groups or Nextdoor for neighborhood recommendations.
- Ask friends, neighbors, or your building manager for referrals.

What to check before hiring
- License and insurance: ask for proof of general liability and worker’s comp.
- Experience and specialties: residential vs commercial; interior-only or full remodels.
- Portfolio: recent photos of finished interiors in similar homes.
- References: get 2–3 recent customer references and follow up.
- Written estimate: detailed line items (prep, number of coats, paint brand and finish, trim/doors).
- Warranty: ask about workmanship guarantees and paint warranty.
- Timeline and cleanup: start/end dates, daily working hours, dust and dropcloth protocols.
- Payment terms: deposit amount, progress payments, final payment conditions.

Questions to ask prospective painters (phone or in-person)
1. Are you licensed/insured? Can I see certificates?
2. How many years have you been painting interiors in St. Louis?
3. Can you provide three recent references and photos of similar projects?
4. What brand and sheen of paint do you use? Is low-VOC available?
5. How many coats are included? Do you prime?
6. How do you handle repairs (holes, cracks, molding) and are those included or extra?
7. What is your projected timeline and crew size?
8. Do you provide a written contract and a warranty?

Red flags
- No written estimate or contract.
- Requests for a large cash-only deposit or payment before work begins without documentation.
- Poor or nonexistent references, or lots of recent negative reviews mentioning missed deadlines or sloppy prep.
- Vague answers about paint brands/coats/priming.

Sample phone script
“Hi — I’m getting quotes to paint the interior of a [house/condo] at [ZIP]. It’s about [# rooms/sq ft]. Do you do interior work in my area? Can you tell me what’s included in a typical estimate (prep, priming, number of coats, paint brand)? Are you licensed and insured? Can you provide references and a sample contract?”

If you want, I can:
- Draft an email or text you can send to painters requesting bids.
- Help you compare 3–4 written estimates (if you paste them here).
- Suggest typical ballpark pricing after you tell me scope and ZIP code.

Tell me your ZIP code and a little about the job and I’ll help shortlist questions and prepare an RFQ or compare bids.
